subject: Clarify monthly remedy calculation & exception language — Octane Health
messages:
From: Erin Park <erin.park@octanehealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@octanehealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on monthly remedy & maintenance carve-outs

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier today. The technical team liked the latency profile, but procurement has a couple of follow-ups before we can move to signature. Two specific items: 1) How exactly would monthly service credits be calculated if we hit a partial degradation — is it pro-rata on downtime minutes or a banded %? 2) We need clearer language that routine maintenance (scheduled windows) and brief rolling upgrades are carve-outs — we can tolerate short hits during those windows but want the math to be explicit.

I've attached the vendor's standard template and our procurement playbook for reference. Could you send a short note explaining your proposed remedy math and an example month calculation? Also, if you can indicate any flexibility on the monthly cap for credits (our target is a single-digit % of the monthly committed spend), that helps us finalize.

Best,
Erin

Attachments: Octane_SLA_Expectations.pdf (pdf), Procure_Playbook_2026.pdf (pdf)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Erin Park <erin.park@octanehealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on monthly remedy & maintenance carve-outs

Erin —

Appreciate the clear asks. Summary answer up front: our template uses a banded monthly remedy calculation tied to uptime percentage (band A/B/C) and pays credits pro-rata within the band, with a hard monthly cap expressed as a % of committed monthly invoice. Routine scheduled maintenance (with >48h notice) and short rolling upgrades (under the scheduled window) are explicitly carved out and do not count toward uptime calculations.

Attached is a short worked example (credit_calculator.xlsx) that models three scenarios: 1) 99.98% uptime (no credit), 2) 99.50% uptime (band B → X% credit prorated), 3) regional service degradation for 3 hours (shows pro-rata minutes and resulting credit). For Octane, given your ask for a single-digit cap, we can offer a 5% monthly cap on credits at the committed spend tier you mentioned in the RFP.

Next steps I propose:
- We share the redline of our Redwood_SLA_Template_v2.docx with explicit maintenance carve-out wording and the cap term.
- Loop in Karthik (legal) and Markus (infra) to confirm carve-out thresholds and whether the 48h notice clause is sufficient operationally.

I cc'd them on this reply. If that works I'll send the redline by tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Schedule: https://calendly.com/tessa-morgan/30

Attachments: credit_calculator.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T08:41:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Clarify monthly remedy calculation & exception language — Octane Health

Tessa / team —

Quick read of the proposed approach: banded credits + pro-rata within band + hard monthly cap is acceptable commercially. A couple of legal points to confirm before we send a redline to Erin:
1) Define "scheduled maintenance": proposing "maintenance windows scheduled at least 48 hours in advance and not exceeding 6 hours per week on a rolling basis" — Markus, can ops commit to that?
2) Add a clause about "good-faith mitigation" — Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate and will provide post-incident reports that show the mitigation steps (this helps limit dispute volume).
3) For the cap, prefer expressing it as "no more than 5% of the monthly committed invoice" rather than a dollar cap (keeps it simple).

Markus — any pushback on the durations or the reporting ask?

Thanks,
Karthik
General Counsel (acting) — Legal Ops

All —

Ops can work with the 48h notice for planned maintenance; want to flag two operational realities: 1) for critical security fixes we may need an emergency maintenance clause that allows <48h action — propose an emergency carve-out (with post-notification and report). 2) rolling upgrades across regional pools may create short-lived KV-cache cold-starts that look like brief latency spikes but do not materially affect throughput. Suggest language: "brief latency spikes under 5 minutes per rolling sub-window are not considered downtime for remedy calculation if overall request success rate >= 99.9% for the minute-level aggregation."

I'll draft a short infra note and attach to the redline.

-Markus
VP, Infrastructure

Attachments: ops_maintenance_guidance.txt (text)

Subject: Re: Clarify monthly remedy calculation & exception language — Octane Health

Tessa, Karthik, Markus —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the worked example. We reviewed internally. A few follow-ups from procurement and SRE:

- The 5% monthly cap is in the range we expected — procurement can accept that if we add language that ensures credits are applied as a refund on the following invoice rather than a service credit that needs a separate reconciliation.
- The 48h notice for scheduled maintenance is acceptable; however, our SRE team asked that emergency maintenance be limited to true security incidents and that Redwood include the incident classification rubric in the appendix (so we can avoid disputes on what qualifies).
- On rolling upgrades: their concern is operational visibility. Can you include a clause that mandates a 7-day change log for any rolling upgrade that may affect latency (so they can triage quickly)?

If you can incorporate these three items into the redline we should be able to move to signature quickly. Also cc'ing Jamie who will own procurement sign-off.

Best,
Erin

1) Cap application: we will state credits are applied as a refund (invoice credit applied to next invoice) rather than a separate reconciliation line.
2) Emergency maintenance: carve-out limited to "critical security incidents" with a defined incident classification rubric in the appendix (we will draft the rubric and include it in the redline).
3) Rolling upgrade visibility: we will add the 7-day change log requirement and a one-page ops playbook describing our rolling upgrade steps and monitoring hooks.

I attached the redline of Redwood_SLA_Template_v2.docx with the new language and the updated credit_calculator.xlsx showing the refund flow. Please review — if this aligns I'll coordinate legal to deliver the final DocuSign package by Friday. If you want to hop on a 20-minute call to walk through the redline we'll do that as well.

Next steps for us: Karthik will finalize the legal phrasing and Laura will coordinate the DocuSign workflow. Markus will prepare the ops appendix and the 7-day change log template.

Thanks again — looking forward to closing this for Octane.

Best,
